## Introduction

In the final five minutes, we will discuss what another researcher
needs to rerun or verify our analysis. If time allows, the instructor
will show a distribution comparison from *synthpop* and a model
version history from *vetiver*. The code below is for follow-up with
the prepared workshop environment.

## Prepare the study summaries

We will use the saved pin identifier for the full 29-study dataset.
Run the setup from the project root with *box* and *pins*. Use the
versions CSV and board from the dataset versioning exercise.
[Dataset storage and versioning](05_pins.qmd#pins-checkpoint)

```{r health-extras-data, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
box::use(pins[board_folder, pin_read], utils[read.csv])

workshop_dir <- file.path("outputs", "health-wellbeing")
versions <- read.csv(
  file.path(workshop_dir, "dataset-versions.csv"),
  colClasses = "character"
)
full_version <- versions$version[versions$scope == "all"]
stopifnot(length(full_version) == 1L)

data_board <- board_folder(
  file.path(workshop_dir, "data_store"),
  versioned = TRUE
)
health_full <- pin_read(
  data_board, "health_wellbeing", version = full_version
)
stopifnot(nrow(health_full) == 29L)

original <- data.frame(
  population = factor(health_full$population),
  z = atanh(health_full$cor),
  log_n = log(health_full$n)
)
```

`z` is the Fisher transformation of the correlation, and `log_n`
is the natural log of the study sample size. The example uses
study summaries and leaves out the original study labels and country
column.

## Synthetic study summaries

With *synthpop* available, we will use the CART synthesis method and
seed 123 so we can repeat the classroom run in the same environment.
We convert the generated values to the original scales and give
the new rows synthetic labels. The generated sample sizes describe
synthetic rows.

```{r health-synthetic-data, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
box::use(synthpop[compare, syn])

synthetic <- syn(
  original,
  method = "cart",
  seed = 123,
  print.flag = FALSE
)

synthetic_data <- data.frame(
  author = sprintf("Synthetic %02d", seq_len(nrow(synthetic$syn))),
  cor = tanh(synthetic$syn$z),
  n = round(exp(synthetic$syn$log_n)),
  population = synthetic$syn$population
)
head(synthetic_data)
compare(synthetic, original)
```

Inspect the distributions of `population`, `z`, and `log_n`.
The comparison describes the resemblance of the two tables on these
variables. Similar marginals can coexist with differences in their
relationships and in downstream estimates. Treat this as a public
teaching example. A privacy guarantee would require a validated
mechanism and accounting beyond this distribution comparison
[@near2021-synthetic-data]. For the synthesis methods, see
@nowok2016-synthpop and the
[synthpop documentation](https://www.synthpop.org.uk/).

## Model versioning

We will use *vetiver* and *pins* to store two illustrative linear
regressions under the same model name. The second adds log sample
size as a predictor. Both regressions give each study equal weight
and serve to illustrate model versioning. The core meta-analysis
uses study precision and between-study variance when pooling effects.

Reuse the local model board across renders and keep the version
identifiers for each pair of fits. Cached model chunks reuse their
recorded identifiers. Refreshing the cache fits a new pair and retains
earlier versions in the board. Keep the board with its document cache;
if you remove the board, refresh the cache when rendering again.

```{r health-vetiver-setup, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
box::use(
  pins[pin_exists, pin_versions],
  stats[lm],
  vetiver[vetiver_model, vetiver_pin_write, vetiver_pin_read]
)

model_board <- board_folder(
  file.path(workshop_dir, "model_store"),
  versioned = TRUE
)
model_name <- "health_wellbeing"

model_source <- list(
  data_version = full_version,
  r_version = as.character(getRversion()),
  vetiver_version = as.character(utils::packageVersion("vetiver"))
)
```

```{r health-vetiver-versions, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = TRUE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE, cache.extra = get0("model_source")}
previous_versions <- if (pin_exists(model_board, model_name)) {
  pin_versions(model_board, model_name)$version
} else {
  character()
}

model_v1 <- lm(z ~ population, data = original)
v1 <- vetiver_model(
  model_v1,
  model_name = model_name,
  description = "Illustrative regression on population.",
  metadata = model_source
)
vetiver_pin_write(model_board, v1)
first_version <- setdiff(
  pin_versions(model_board, model_name)$version, previous_versions
)
stopifnot(length(first_version) == 1L)

model_v2 <- lm(z ~ population + log_n, data = original)
v2 <- vetiver_model(
  model_v2,
  model_name = model_name,
  description = "Illustrative regression on population and log sample size.",
  metadata = model_source
)
vetiver_pin_write(model_board, v2)

model_history <- pin_versions(model_board, model_name)
second_version <- setdiff(
  model_history$version, c(previous_versions, first_version)
)
stopifnot(length(first_version) == 1L, length(second_version) == 1L)
model_history
```

When you use `vetiver_pin_read()` without a version, it selects the
board's current version. Pass an explicit identifier when you want
to reproduce a previous prediction or inspect its input requirements.
Compare the input columns of the two retrieved models.

```{r health-vetiver-read, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = TRUE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE, cache.extra = list(get0("first_version"), get0("second_version"))}
stored_v1 <- vetiver_pin_read(
  model_board, model_name, version = first_version
)
stored_v2 <- vetiver_pin_read(
  model_board, model_name, version = second_version
)
names(stored_v1$prototype)
names(stored_v2$prototype)
stored_v2$metadata
```

The model's metadata retains its training pin version and software
context [@vetiver-pin-write]. Keep the fitted objects and generated tables
local until you have checked applicable release terms.

## Concluding discussion {#extras-discussion}

-   If you received only the report, which versions and files would
    you ask for to rerun it?
-   If the original data could not be shared, what could a reader
    test with a synthetic dataset, and what would require access to
    the originals?
-   Which single change would make your own research workflow easier
    for a collaborator to inspect and rerun?

A useful checkpoint is to point to the exact data version, analysis
revision, environment, and archive citation for one reported result.
If you try the optional model exercise, check that the first model
expects `population` and the second also expects `log_n`.
